partial_case.facts: The resident is a secure tenant of the landlord which is a local authority. The tenancy started on 17 September 2012. The property is a 1 bedroom ground floor flat in a purpose-built block. The landlord is aware that the resident has vulnerabilities, including mobility issues. The landlord carried out property inspections during March and June 2024. It identified a schedule of works which included the shower enclosure in the wet room. On 21 June the resident emailed the landlord to ask to delay works. Works commenced during August. On 23 September the resident moved to temporary accommodation. Works were completed in October 2024. On 23 August 2024 the resident raised a formal complaint about boxes left around her home that meant she was unable to safely move around, lack of help with packing, works not matching what the surveyor agreed, poor monitoring, inconsistent communication, operatives walking into her home without introducing themselves, and her disability and mobility issues being ignored. On 9 September 2024 the landlord issued its stage 1 response. On 17 September 2024 the resident escalated her complaint. On 18 October 2024 the landlord issued its stage 2 complaint response offering £225 compensation. On 21 October 2024 the resident asked the Housing Ombudsman to investigate her complaint.
partial_case.ground_truth_outcome: Maladministration found in both repairs handling and complaint handling. Landlord ordered to pay £500 compensation (£400 for repairs failures, £100 for complaint handling failures), provide written apology, clarify shower access issues, and conduct case review.

It failed to proactively monitor and manage the repairs and temporary accommodation process.
It failed to communicate effectively with the resident.
There were record keeping failures which impacted on our assessment of the landlord's response.
The landlord failed to comply with all the requirements of the Code.
It failed to demonstrate that it had carried out a thorough investigate of the complaint.
